title: pH-sensitive smart textile
summary: A reversible colour response using roselle-derived anthocyanin on cotton.
body:
A cotton fabric designed to visibly respond to changes in its chemical environment, using anthocyanin extracted from roselle.

What the project explored

The fabric showed a reversible colour response across acidic, neutral, and alkaline environments. The lab work examined how mordant concentration and thermal processing could improve wash-fastness performance.

From testing to documentation

The work included colour-response testing and a complete experimental record covering the methodology, observations, and analysis.

This was a coursework project for the Wet Processing II Lab in 2025.
